paper_title: The Unseen Targets of Hate -- A Systematic Review of Hateful   Communication Datasets
caption: Single vs. multiple platforms as data sources over time. While most of the datasets are collected from a single source, around 2018 researchers are increasingly collecting data from multiple sources (i.e., two or more).
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates how many hateful communication datasets per year are collected from a single data source versus from multiple data sources (two or more) over the period shown. The horizontal axis contains the categorical years in chronological order from 2012 through 2022 and is labeled “Year.” The vertical axis is labeled “Number of datasets,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to slightly above 110, with regularly spaced tick marks and gridlines at 20-unit intervals (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). For each year, two adjacent bars are shown as a grouped pair: a blue bar for “1” and an orange bar for “2+,” as indicated by the legend titled “Data sources.” The earliest years have very small counts (e.g., around 2 datasets for “2+” in 2012, around 2 for “1” in 2013, around 3 for “1” in 2014, and around 2 for “2+” in 2015), followed by larger values in later years, such as approximately 10 (“1”) and 3 (“2+”) in 2016; about 22 (“1”) and 6 (“2+”) in 2017; about 30 (“1”) and 18 (“2+”) in 2018; about 46 (“1”) and 19 (“2+”) in 2019; about 87 (“1”) and 43 (“2+”) in 2020; and the tallest bars in 2021 at roughly 112 for “1” and 47 for “2+.” In 2022, the two bars appear in lighter tints of the same colors (light blue and light orange) rather than the darker palette used earlier, with approximate values near 30 for “1” and about 7 for “2+.” The bars are not sorted by height; they follow the year sequence, and aside from the lighter shading in 2022, there is no additional outlining or annotation emphasizing particular bars.
